culturalBackground: Gulf-style, or Khaleeji, henna is popular in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman.
It is known for large, bold flowers and leaves with plenty of open space between them.
Designs usually flow diagonally across the hand instead of covering it completely.
A henna night before the wedding is a long-standing custom in Gulf weddings.
applicationTips: Use a slightly wider cone tip to get the thick outlines that define the Gulf look.
Leave clear gaps between motifs; the empty space is part of the style.
Fill petals with shading instead of fine detail to keep the design bold.

faqPool.a: It is the henna style of the Arabian Gulf countries: bold floral motifs with thick outlines and open space.

faqPool.q: How is Gulf henna different from Indian mehndi?
faqPool.a: Gulf designs are larger and more open, while Indian mehndi is finer and covers more of the skin.

faqPool.q: Is Gulf-style henna quick to apply?
faqPool.a: Usually, yes. The larger motifs and open spacing mean a hand can be finished much faster than a dense design.
